description:
FILED s451w, from the #694 probes.  PRE-EXISTING (identical on 718db6b and on
the f937afd pre-round-9 base).

perl's `` `CMD` `` and `qx{CMD}` are `readpipe CMD`, and `readpipe` is
overridable -- t/op/exec.t:158 does exactly that:

    package o {
        use subs "readpipe";
        sub readpipe { pop }
        ::is `${\"hello"}`, 'hello', 'overridden `` interpolates [perl #115330]';
    }

MEASURED (s451w probe, `sub readpipe { return "OVR:" . pop }` in package o):

    form            perl            PCL
    `simple`        OVR:simple      (empty -- ran the shell, command not found)
    `has$v`         OVR:hasiv       (empty)
    qx{qxform}      OVR:qxform      (empty)
    <<`H`           OVR:heredociv   heredociv  (see #702 -- not executed at all)

So the whole `p-backtick` lowering goes straight to the shell.  perl's rule:
the interpolated string is the ARGUMENT to `readpipe`, and if the current
package has a `readpipe` sub declared with `use subs` (or imported), that sub
is called instead of the builtin -- exactly the override mechanism PCL already
implements for other overridable builtins.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): `p-backtick`'s emission should ask the same
"is this builtin overridden HERE" question the compiler already asks for other
core-overridable names, and lower to a call when it is.  Grep for how `use
subs` is recorded (Pl::Environment) and for the existing override dispatch
before writing anything -- rule 11 says route through it rather than adding a
backtick-only branch.

BAR: the four-row table above vs perl; a NON-overriding package still runs the
shell; the override is LEXICAL/PACKAGE-scoped, so a second package in the same
file must still run the shell (probe it); t/op/exec.t rows 31-32.  #702 (the
backtick heredoc is not executed at all) is the sibling and should be measured
together -- row 32 currently passes only because the two bugs cancel.
CLOSED s451z.  `use subs LIST` is recorded per PACKAGE with its SOURCE
POSITION in `Pl::Environment` (`add_builtin_override` /
`builtin_is_overridden`), by a PRE-PASS `Parser2::_premerge_use_subs` -- not at
the statement, because a named sub's BODY is lowered first and a backtick
inside a sub then silently ran the shell.  A command capture in an overriding
package lowers to a plain funcall node on `PKG::readpipe`, so call-site context
comes free.

PROBED vs 5.40.3, all identical after: ``/qx/`` <<`` ``/explicit call in the
overriding package; a SECOND package in the same file still runs the shell;
re-entering the declaring package re-enables it; a plain `sub readpipe` with NO
`use subs` does NOT override; a backtick BEFORE the `use subs` is still the
builtin; the override reaches a backtick inside a named sub body.

`_parse_use_import_list` gained an OPT-IN `bare_quote` arm for the
unparenthesised `use subs "readpipe";` spelling.  Making it unconditional is
WRONG and was measured so -- see #733.

t/op/exec.t rows 31-32 now transpile to `(o::pl-readpipe â¦)`; the file still
aborts before them at `system "lskdfj"` (the `aborted-forms` signature), so its
suite verdict does not move on this change alone.

RESIDUE, filed: #732 (a plain sub still captures the builtin, and `CORE::` is
stripped), #734 (`readpipe` as a NAME is not implemented at all).
subject: `use subs "readpipe"` does not override backticks / qx -- PCL always runs the shell where perl calls the user's sub (t/op/exec.t rows 31-32, [perl #115330])
